JLPT Mock Exam Guide: Realistic Timing, Scoring and Review

Kanjidon Team · Mar 16, 2026

A mock exam is useful when it recreates the current timing, exposes a specific weakness and leads to correction. It is not useful when a raw percentage is treated as an official JLPT score or when repeated simulations replace learning. This guide shows how to run one diagnostic mock, review it properly and decide what to do next.

Current Official Test Times

LevelTimed sectionsTotal
N5Vocabulary 20 min; Grammar and Reading 40 min; Listening 30 min90 min
N4Vocabulary 25 min; Grammar and Reading 55 min; Listening 35 min115 min
N3Vocabulary 30 min; Grammar and Reading 70 min; Listening 40 min140 min
N2Language Knowledge and Reading 105 min; Listening 50 min155 min
N1Language Knowledge and Reading 110 min; Listening 55 min165 min

Use the times for your target level, but remember that a home simulation cannot reproduce venue procedures, breaks, room noise or every official testing condition.

Use Official Question Types as the Reference

The JLPT publishes the composition of test items, sample questions and Official Practice Workbooks. Those are the best references for current format. Practice providers can write similar tasks, but they should not claim that their questions are secret past papers or identical to the live exam.

Set Up One Diagnostic Mock

  • Choose fresh material you have not memorised.
  • Use the official time for each test section and follow its order.
  • Remove dictionaries, notes, pausing and replay unless the practice instructions explicitly allow them.
  • Mark guesses without changing the answer after checking a later clue.
  • Record interruptions so you can distinguish a study issue from a broken simulation.

Score It Honestly

Count raw correct answers only as a practice metric. Official JLPT results use scaled scores, and the relationship between raw responses and the reported score is not a simple one-point-per-question conversion. Compare your raw performance across equivalent practice sets, not directly with 80, 90, 95 or 100 on the official 180-point scale.

Remember the Sectional Minimums

LevelsOverall pass markSection minimums
N580/18038/120 Language Knowledge and Reading; 19/60 Listening
N490/18038/120 Language Knowledge and Reading; 19/60 Listening
N395/18019/60 in Language Knowledge, Reading and Listening
N290/18019/60 in Language Knowledge, Reading and Listening
N1100/18019/60 in Language Knowledge, Reading and Listening

These are official result requirements, not raw mock cutoffs. Their practical lesson is that one neglected section can prevent a pass even when the overall result is strong.

Review Every Error by Cause

Error typeQuestion to askNext action
Knowledge gapWas the word, kanji or grammar pattern unknown?Learn it in context and schedule retrieval
Misread promptDid you answer a different question?Underline task words during review
Reading processDid you lose the topic, reference or contrast?Practise shorter passages with structure notes
Listening processDid you miss the task, speaker or key detail?Use transcript-assisted correction, then retry without text
PacingWas the answer possible but unfinished?Practise that item type under a smaller time limit
GuessingWas the correct response unsupported?Do not count a lucky answer as mastered

Kanjidon Practice Bank: What the Number Means

The Kanjidon content snapshot reviewed for this article contains 10,083 local practice records: 2,279 tagged N5, 1,595 N4, 1,878 N3, 2,235 N2 and 2,096 N1. This is the size of an app practice bank, not a claim that the JLPT has 10,083 official questions. Records can repeat skills or formats, and a large pool does not by itself validate difficulty or scoring.

What Kanjidon Simulates

Kanjidon can assemble level-specific, timed, multi-section practice from its local bank and report your practice performance. Use it to rehearse pacing and locate weak topics. Its score is not the JLPT’s official scaled result, its prompts are not live exam questions, and you should also use the official samples and practice workbooks.

When to Take the Next Mock

Take another full simulation after you have acted on the previous error profile and can use fresh material. Between mocks, targeted practice usually produces more information than repeatedly measuring the same weakness. As test day approaches, full timing becomes more valuable for endurance and transitions.

  • Official JLPT FAQ: scaled scores
